newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Metrobank Q1 net up at 1.25 bln pesos. [CORRECTED 11:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Metrobank Q1 net up at 1.25 bln pesos. [CORRECTED 11:20 GMT]

text.p: Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co (Metrobank) said on Tuesday its net income in the first three months (corrects from "first three quarters") reached 1.25 billion pesos compared to 1.0 billion a year ago.
Net income in the first three months would have been higher at 1.75 billion pesos but it decided to book reserves of 500 million pesos in the interests of prudent banking, it said.
"This move to boost the bank's reserves, in the interest of conservative and prudent banking, brings the bank's total reserves for non-performing assets to 2.1 billion pesos," the bank said.
"This is a billion more than the reserves required by the Philippine Central Bank," it added.
As of March 20, 1997, the bank said it had the biggest loan portfolio in the domestic banking industry at 138.56 billion pesos and the largest amount of deposits at 149.18 billion pesos.
It is also the largest-capitalised bank with a net worth of 33.34 billion pesos as of March 20.
Its consolidated assets, the highest also in the industry, stood at 231.9 billion pesos during the first quarter, 4.3 percent higher than the end-1996 level of 222.3 billion.
The bank earlier said it expected a net income of 6.65 billion pesos this year, 33 percent higher than five billion pesos last year.
